  <section v="12">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Every descent is for the sake of an ascent, as the soul's descent elevates it higher than before, and likewise the descent of the worlds through the chain of progression leads to the creation of this lowly world specifically for the purpose of making a dwelling place for the Awtsmoos.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, it is known that every descent is for the sake of an ascent.</t>
    <t s="2">For the descent of the soul below is in order that through this the soul will be elevated to a level higher than it was prior to its descent below33,</t>
    <t s="3">And so too is it with the descent</t>
    <t s="4">(and the chain of progression)</t>
    <t s="5">of the worlds,</t>
    <t s="6">that they descended from level to level</t>
    <t s="7">(from world to world)</t>
    <t s="8">until this lowly world came into being from them,</t>
    <t s="9">it is for the sake of the ascent that is accomplished through this34</t>
    <t s="10">[for specifically this lowly world is a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="11">a dwelling place for the Awtsmoos].</t>
    <t s="12">And from this it is understood,</t>
    <t s="13">that so too is it regarding the descent within this world itself,</t>
    <t s="14">that the descent that occurred in it through the sin of the Tree of Knowledge and the undesirable matters that followed it is for the sake of an ascent,</t>
    <t s="15">in order that the drawing down of the principal Shechinah below now</t>
    <t s="16">(after it was removed)</t>
    <t s="17">will be more elevated than the drawing down of the principal Shechinah in the lower realms that was at the beginning of creation.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="13">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>One might think that a descent caused by sin, being contrary to the divine will, is not necessarily for the sake of an ascent, but the fact that human choice only affects the speed of fulfilling the purpose proves that the removal of the principal Shechinah was only temporary, yet it does not prove that the subsequent drawing down is more elevated.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And superficially, one could say,</t>
    <t s="1">that this [principle] that a descent is for the sake of an ascent applies when the descent is in His will, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="2">[for then one must say,</t>
    <t s="3">that the desire for the descent is for the sake of the ascent that comes through the descent].</t>
    <t s="4">However, a descent that comes through sin,</t>
    <t s="5">which is contrary to the will of the Supernal One</t>

    <t s="7">there is no necessity, seemingly, that even this descent is for the sake of an ascent.</t>
    <t s="8">And although it is not possible that man's choice should prevent, heaven forbid, the completion of the intention of a dwelling place in the lower realms35,</t>
    <t s="9">and man's choice only determines the speed of the completion of the intention36,</t>
    <t s="10">from this it is proven,</t>
    <t s="11">that the removal of the principal Shechinah that came about through the sin of the Tree of Knowledge and the sins that followed it was</t>
    <t s="12">(from the outset)</t>
    <t s="13">only temporary,</t>
    <t s="14">now, this matter is only a proof that this [fact] that through the sins the principal Shechinah was removed was</t>
    <t s="15">(from the outset)</t>
    <t s="16">only temporary,</t>
    <t s="17">and necessarily afterwards there will be a drawing down of the principal Shechinah below.</t>
    <t s="18">But,</t>
    <t s="19">what is the proof that the drawing down below after the removal is more elevated than the drawing down that was at the beginning of creation?</t>
  </section>
  <section v="14">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The Midrash states that the blame for death is attributed to Adam, yet the Torah preceded the world and speaks of death, and the Mitteler Rebbe explains that this attribution applies also to the sin itself, for the evil inclination is incited from above, and since the descent caused by the sin of the Tree of Knowledge was intentional, it must be for the sake of an ascent to a higher level.</sectionSummaryBrief>

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Every descent is for the sake of an ascent, as the soul's descent elevates it higher than before, and likewise the descent of the worlds through the chain of progression leads to the creation of this lowly world specifically for the purpose of making a dwelling place for the Awtsmoos.

translations.translation: Now, it is known that every descent is for the sake of an ascent.
For the descent of the soul below is in order that through this the soul will be elevated to a level higher than it was prior to its descent below33,
And so too is it with the descent
(and the chain of progression)
of the worlds,
that they descended from level to level
(from world to world)
until this lowly world came into being from them,
it is for the sake of the ascent that is accomplished through this34
[for specifically this lowly world is a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He,
a dwelling place for the Awtsmoos].
And from this it is understood,
that so too is it regarding the descent within this world itself,
that the descent that occurred in it through the sin of the Tree of Knowledge and the undesirable matters that followed it is for the sake of an ascent,
in order that the drawing down of the principal Shechinah below now
(after it was removed)
will be more elevated than the drawing down of the principal Shechinah in the lower realms that was at the beginning of creation.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: One might think that a descent caused by sin, being contrary to the divine will, is not necessarily for the sake of an ascent, but the fact that human choice only affects the speed of fulfilling the purpose proves that the removal of the principal Shechinah was only temporary, yet it does not prove that the subsequent drawing down is more elevated.

translations.translation: And superficially, one could say,
that this [principle] that a descent is for the sake of an ascent applies when the descent is in His will, blessed be He,
[for then one must say,
that the desire for the descent is for the sake of the ascent that comes through the descent].
However, a descent that comes through sin,
which is contrary to the will of the Supernal One
[for through the power of choice given to man, he has the ability to choose contrary to the will and intention for which he was created],
there is no necessity, seemingly, that even this descent is for the sake of an ascent.
And although it is not possible that man's choice should prevent, heaven forbid, the completion of the intention of a dwelling place in the lower realms35,
and man's choice only determines the speed of the completion of the intention36,
from this it is proven,
that the removal of the principal Shechinah that came about through the sin of the Tree of Knowledge and the sins that followed it was
(from the outset)
only temporary,
now, this matter is only a proof that this [fact] that through the sins the principal Shechinah was removed was
(from the outset)
only temporary,
and necessarily afterwards there will be a drawing down of the principal Shechinah below.
But,
what is the proof that the drawing down below after the removal is more elevated than the drawing down that was at the beginning of creation?

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The Midrash states that the blame for death is attributed to Adam, yet the Torah preceded the world and speaks of death, and the Mitteler Rebbe explains that this attribution applies also to the sin itself, for the evil inclination is incited from above, and since the descent caused by the sin of the Tree of Knowledge was intentional, it must be for the sake of an ascent to a higher level.

translations.translation: And the explanation is,
that it is stated in the Midrash37
on the verse38
"Nora alilah al bnei adam,"
"Alilah" is attributed to him
(to Adam the first)
that he brought death to the world
(for "on the day you eat from it you shall surely die"39),
for the Torah preceded the world by two thousand years and it is written in it40
"Zot haTorah, adam ki yamut b'ohel."
And the Mitteler Rebbe explains41,
that this [matter] that "alilah" is attributed to him
(to Adam the first)
is not only regarding the death that came through the sin of the Tree of Knowledge, but also regarding the sin itself.
For that which sometimes the evil of the evil inclination overcomes a person,
is because from above the evil inclination was incited against him to bring him to this sin.
[However, the assistance from above for the evil in a person to overcome the good in him,
and likewise the assistance from above for the good in a person to overcome the evil in him,
is separate from the person and is not felt by him,
and therefore it does not compel the person,
and that which a person chooses good or evil is free choice].
And since the descent of the world
(the removal of the principal Shechinah)
that came about through the sin of the Tree of Knowledge
(even though the sin is contrary to the will)
was intentional,
it must be said,
that the intention of the descent is for the sake of an ascent,
in order that the drawing down of the principal Shechinah after it was removed will be more elevated than it was at the beginning of creation.
